scope: .vite/build/*.js in frozen extraction; complete selected entry/bootstrap/startup/loader functions and direct env-name usage

conclusions.claim: No genuine supported shell-env skip/disable flag was identified in the traced startup path. The entry/initializer unconditionally execute it. This is a scoped static conclusion, not a guarantee that an undocumented native flag cannot exist.

Launch-time FORCE_CLI and CODEX_CLI_PATH are inherited by the shell child through execa extendEnv=true. If shell initialization leaves them unchanged, they survive; shell exports can override them before routing/runtime resolution.
Only CODEX_HOME has explicit restoration after shell import, conditional on an initially nonempty CODEX_ELECTRON_USER_DATA_PATH. FORCE_CLI, CLI_PATH and USER_DATA_PATH lack equivalent protection.
CODEX_SHELL is a marker passed to shell loading, not a shell selection or disable control. SHELL alone is insufficient because os.userInfo().shell is preferred.

stageOrder: startup module captures initial CODEX_HOME only if initial explicit userData env is set
initializeNodeNetworkPermissions calls Gi/Ki/qi and imports interactive login shell environment
Object.assign(process.env, shellEnv); protected CODEX_HOME restoration only
prepare/read startup requirements uses current env for CLI/network-policy preparation
bootstrap imports and explicitly sets Electron userData from current env
main routing reads current FORCE_CLI; runtime resolver reads current CLI_PATH; spawn environment spreads current process.env

controls.readPhase: before shell import to protect CODEX_HOME; after shell import to set userData
controls.guarantee: Protects original CODEX_HOME only. Verify final userData if shell scripts could redefine userData env.

controls.readPhase: after shell import at transport/routing selection
controls.guarantee: Disables WebSocket and local daemon candidates only if effective current value remains 1.

controls.readPhase: after shell import at CLI runtime resolution
controls.guarantee: Pins executable only if effective current value remains intended path; host codex_cli_command can be an earlier override.

controls.readPhase: native Chromium launch; JS subsequently calls app.setPath(userData, oD(...))
controls.guarantee: Used in demo launcher but not evidence of effective final userData without verification.

controls.readPhase: set internally as extraEnv on shell loader
controls.guarantee: Marker only; no built-in disable branch found.

independentLaunchLimits: Clearing inherited CODEX_* before launch reduces parent session coupling; startup shell may reintroduce any exported CODEX_* or auth variables.
Force CLI plus frozen CLI_PATH require post-hydration executable/transport observation. Never infer them from launch argv alone.
Separate profile and Codex home do not exclude native keyring or encrypted secret storage; exact active backend remains unresolved.
A test OS account with no credentials and no personal startup exports supplies stronger evidence; no such test was performed here.
No fake skip-shell-env flag should be used. If a task-owned instrumented clone protects additional env keys, document that source modification and do not call it unmodified baseline behavior.

evidence.claim: Bootstrap computes userData from current CODEX_ELECTRON_USER_DATA_PATH; original value is not separately restored by shell loader.
Single-instance behavior uses explicit userData path; unrelated to credential isolation.
Application actively sets userData using oD after shell hydration; --user-data-dir alone does not prove final effective profile.
FORCE_CLI=1 also excludes local-daemon selection condition; read after awaited CLI preparation.
